usageNotes: Use this to append a new firewall rule to an existing cluster-level security group; the security group must already exist (create it first via POST /cluster/firewall/groups). Requires 'Sys.Modify' on the root path, so only cluster administrators can call it. Rules are appended at the end by default — use 'pos' to insert at a specific position, keeping in mind that rules are evaluated top-down.

examples.summary: Block inbound SSH from the internet to any VM in the 'external-vms' security group, logged at warning level

params.comment: Block inbound SSH from untrusted sources

tips: The 'group' path parameter must match an existing security group name (2–18 chars, starts with a letter); creating a rule against a non-existent group returns an error.
Omitting 'enable' leaves the rule disabled by default in some PVE versions — explicitly set enable=1 to activate immediately.
Use the 'macro' field (e.g., 'SSH', 'HTTP', 'HTTPS') to apply predefined port+protocol combinations instead of manually setting proto/dport.
Set 'digest' to the current ruleset digest to guard against concurrent edits overwriting each other in multi-admin environments.
Rules referencing IP sets must prefix the set name with '+' (e.g., '+trusted-hosts') and the IP set must already exist at the cluster firewall level.
